question: A 38-year-old man presents with pruritus and jaundice. Past medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis diagnosed 2 years ago, well managed medically. He is vaccinated against hepatitis A and B and denies any recent travel abroad. On physical examination, prominent hepatosplenomegaly is noted. Which of the following would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "38-year-old man with pruritus and jaundice" -> "history of ulcerative colitis" -> "possible primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)" -> "ERCP can visualize bile ducts" -> "ERCP shows strictures and beading" -> "confirms diagnosis of PSC" -> 85%

CHAIN: "38-year-old man with pruritus and jaundice" -> "prominent hepatosplenomegaly noted" -> "consider liver pathology" -> "ulcerative colitis increases risk of PSC" -> "MRCP can assess bile duct abnormalities" -> "MRCP shows bile duct irregularities" -> "supports diagnosis of PSC" -> 80%

CHAIN: "38-year-old man with pruritus and jaundice" -> "ulcerative colitis history" -> "risk factor for PSC" -> "ERCP is the gold standard for diagnosis" -> "ERCP reveals characteristic findings" -> "confirms PSC diagnosis" -> 90%

CHAIN: "38-year-old man with pruritus and jaundice" -> "hepatosplenomegaly present" -> "consider cholestatic liver disease" -> "MRCP can evaluate biliary tree" -> "MRCP shows abnormalities" -> "suggests PSC" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's presentation of pruritus, jaundice, and hepatosplenomegaly, along with a history of ulcerative colitis, raises suspicion for primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). PSC is often associated with inflammatory bowel disease, particularly ulcerative colitis. To confirm the diagnosis, imaging of the bile ducts is essential. Among the options provided, Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) is the most appropriate non-invasive test to visualize the bile ducts and assess for the characteristic bile duct strictures and beading seen in PSC.
